title: IMO 2026 Autonomous Perfect 42/42 Scores & Full Lean 4 Formalization of All Six Problems
aiSystem: Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol (LeanFlow) & Kimi K3
whyItMatters: One year after the first 35/42 IMO Gold medal, Claude Fable 5 scored a perfect 42/42 autonomously in 1.8 hours, Kimi K3 hit 42/42, and GPT-5.6 Sol formally proved all six IMO 2026 problems end-to-end in Lean 4.
summary: Marking the complete saturation of the world’s hardest high-school mathematics competition just 12 months after IMO 2025’s first AI gold medals (35/42), open GitHub benchmarks on the official IMO 2026 problems demonstrated autonomous perfect 42/42 performance and full formalization across multiple frontier model families. In github.com/deedy/imo-2026 (using a minimal three-tool, network-blocked single-context agent harness), Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5 achieved a verified single-shot 42/42 in just 1.8 hours—including the only fully synthetic P2 geometry proof—while GPT-5.6 Sol and Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 also reached verified 42/42 (Kimi K3 inventing an original compactness theorem for P6). Independently, EPFL’s LARA lab (github.com/epfl-lara/AutoformalizedProjects) used GPT-5.6 Sol with LeanFlow to produce complete, machine-checked Lean 4 formalizations of all six IMO 2026 problems verified together as one Lake project.
technicalHighlights: Claude Fable 5 scored an autonomous, single-shot 42/42 on IMO 2026 in 1.8 hours with no reviewer, orchestration, or internet access.
EPFL LARA’s AutoformalizedProjects verified proof-complete Lean 4 formalizations of all 6 IMO 2026 problems produced autonomously by GPT-5.6 Sol.
Kimi K3 became an open-ecosystem frontier model to reach 42/42 (with review feedback), inventing an original P6 compactness argument.
caveats: The deedy/imo-2026 natural-language scores were graded by automated verifier agents rather than official IMO jury coordinators, whereas EPFL’s GPT-5.6 Sol Lean 4 formalizations of Problems 1–6 are deterministically kernel-checked in Lean.

scoreRationale.foundational: Marks complete saturation (perfect 42/42 and full Lean 4 proof-completeness) of the International Mathematical Olympiad.
scoreRationale.ripple: Demonstrated that gold-plus olympiad reasoning diffused from closed lab harnesses in 2025 to general API models across three labs by mid-2026.
scoreRationale.verification: All six IMO 2026 problems formally verified as one compiled Lean 4 project in EPFL’s public AutoformalizedProjects repository.
scoreRationale.velocity: Jumped from 35/42 (IMO 2025) to single-shot 42/42 in 1.8 hours and full 6/6 Lean formalization within 12 months.
